Removes every trace of metadata, even the orientation tag, so a rotated photo may look sideways afterward. Turns off the keep options below and always fully re-encodes video for the most thorough clean.

When your video is already in a compatible format, Redact strips its metadata with a quick pass instead of fully re-encoding it. That\'s faster and lighter on battery, though a full re-encode removes a touch more. Automatically turned off when Strict Clean is on or when cleaning files shared in from other apps.

resources.string: Redact helps you share photos and videos without sharing your private details. This short tour takes about a minute.
Clean removes the hidden details from your photos and videos.
Scan shows you exactly what a file reveals before you share it.
Convert changes a photo or video to another format and keeps it clean.
Censor covers faces, number plates and anything else in a photo that should stay private.
Your photos and videos can say more than you think.
When you take a photo or video, your phone quietly saves extra information inside the file. Anyone you send the file to may be able to read it.
It can show where you were, sometimes closely enough to find your home.
It can show the date and time you took it.
It can show which phone or camera you used.
Your files never leave your phone.
Redact does all of its work right here on your phone. It saves a clean copy for you to share and leaves your original just as it was.
Nothing is uploaded, so your photos and videos stay private.
There are no ads, and nothing tracks what you do.
Redact is open source, so anyone can check how it works.
You decide what Redact can use.
Next, Redact will explain what it would like to use and why, one thing at a time. It\'s always your choice, and you can change your mind later in Settings.
First, your photos and videos, so Redact can open the ones you pick.
Then, the locations saved in your photos and videos, so Scan can show them to you.
After that, notifications, so Redact can tell you when a task is done.
Allow access to your photos and videos.
Redact needs this to open the photos and videos you choose to clean, scan or convert.
Redact only opens the files you pick.
Your photos and videos stay on your phone.
Android may let you allow only some of your photos and videos. Redact works either way.
You can change this at any time in your phone\'s settings.
See where your photos and videos were taken.

Android hides the location saved in your photos and videos unless you let Redact see it. With this turned on, Scan can show you where a photo or video was taken, so you know what you would be sharing.
This is optional. Redact removes locations from the copies it makes either way.
Redact never shares a location with anyone.
You can turn this off at any time in Settings.
Find out when your files are ready.
Cleaning a long video can take a few minutes. Redact can let you know when it\'s finished, so you don\'t have to keep the app open.
This is optional, and you can turn it off at any time in Settings.
Redact only sends a notification when a task finishes.
Redact never sends ads or reminders.

If Redact ever crashes, it can send an anonymous report so the problem can be found and fixed. Crash reports are the only thing Redact ever sends over the internet.
Reports never include your photos, videos, file names or locations.
Reports go to Sentry, a service that helps developers find and fix crashes.
Last, crash reports, so problems can be found and fixed sooner.
Redact will send anonymous crash reports if something goes wrong.
